newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels defiant despite Mobutu's return.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels defiant despite Mobutu's return.

text.p: Zairean rebels remained defiant despite the return of President Mobutu Sese Seko to Kinshasa on Tuesday and said they were ready for any counter- attack on eastern Zaire.
Gaetan Kakudji, spokesman for Laurent Kabila, the president of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, said Mobutu's return on Tuesday "changes nothing".
"We know he is preparing a counter-attack, but we are confident and prepared to respond," said Kakudji, speaking to Reuters by telephone from Brussels.
"The regime of Mr Mobutu is a sick regime...We need a new man to reconstruct the country," he added.
Mobutu, who has dominated Zaire since seizing power in 1965, returned home to a rapturous welcome from thousands of supporters after four months in Europe where he had surgery for prostate cancer.
Mobutu, 66, was to address the nation later on Tuesday and many Zaireans looked to him to conjure up a solution to end the Tutsi-led revolt in the east which threatens to break up Zaire.

Kakudji said the rebels, who hold a swath of territory about 500 km (300 miles) long from north to south including the main towns of Goma, Bukavu and Uvira, were ready to negotiate with the government but not to declare a unilateral ceasefire.
"He (Kabila) is completely in favour of negotiations at a political level and there has been international pressure, but there is no unilateral ceasefire," Kakudji said.

Eight African leaders who met in Nairobi on Monday urged the warring parties in Zaire to agree to a negotiated peaceful settlement. But Zaire failed to attend the one-day summit because it accuses Rwanda and Uganda of backing the rebels.
Kinshasa last week rejected negotiations with the rebels
The rebels, who launched their revolt in October, say the Zairean army has retreated to its bases at Kindu to the west of Goma while Bunia to the north remains disputed.

Kabila has said they will fight on until they depose Mobutu in Kinshasa but the rebellion has lost its initial momentum in recent weeks with few advances being reported while the Zairean army appears more ready to defend what centres it still holds.
"The rebels control all of North and South Kivu provinces. The question is how far they are prepared to go and what kind of response Kinshasa will offer," said a foreign aid worker.
The rebels have declared a governor for the rebel-held city of Goma bordering on Rwanda and visitors now have their passports stamped: "Democratic Republic of Congo ex Zaire".

At least 5,500 people were killed around Goma in November in fighting between the rebels and Zairean troops and by Rwandan Hutu extremists who killed refugees in an attempt to stop them returning to Rwanda.
More than 600,000 Rwandan refugees have flooded back into Rwanda from eastern Zaire after being forced from their camps by fighting last month, ending two-and-a-half years in exile.
